items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mariano and I went to Europe for … we had a club engagement in Paris for four weeks, and then two weeks in each, one in Copenhagen, and another one in Sweden... Then we went back to Japan again... So we came back to the States at the end of ‟64.

ctx.x: Boo—Boots Mussulli. He was retired and he was from Milford, Massachusetts. And he was … I heard with a small group, recording, you know. He had impeccable technique, but for an Italian, he was very cold, kind of a very intellectual player. It was kind of like totally opposite of somebody like Charlie Mariano, who was much more hot-blooded a player. Boots was much more, kind of, intellectual, cool player, and it was very good for me that he was there. I used to … you know, I used to, when I played, I thought I did…
And so the Storyville, was that something that was arranged through Berklee? Did they arrange…?

items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: as you know I had a quartet at one time with Mariano and so on

ctx.x: Instead of just writing maybe a fairly straight ahead blues chart, you did your own thing.

Yeah, I think at that point I had ten years before that before I came to this country, I had ten years of my career in Japan. And I was doing pretty okay, I got to the point where I was playing probably faster than anybody and longer than anybody. That’s the whole thing. But a big band was something that I wasn’t quite interested in. I was interested in the individual players. I was mainly, and more than anything I was interested in my piano playing to be improved a little more. I sort of thought I could, and I…

became interested in writing much, much later, perhaps ’67, around there. Actually in ’67 I had my own concert, my own produced, to try and get money for work and so on, at the Town Hall and at that time I thought, I was hoping that if some people noticed me, and I had a solo and trio, and about four big band charts. And when I was rehearsing that I felt that’s what I wanted to do. I felt like that’s what I wanted to do. Because up to that point I was getting a little bit of anxiety about the fact that, as you…
